Digital Impression

Digital impressions are a modern alternative to traditional dental impressions. Instead of using trays filled with impression material, the dentist uses an intraoral scanner to capture a 3D image of the teeth and gums. From a patient’s perspective, digital impressions often provide a more comfortable and convenient experience.

1. Improved Comfort

Traditional impressions can be uncomfortable because the tray and material may cause:

* Gag reflex
* Bad taste
* Feeling of pressure
* Difficulty breathing temporarily

Digital impressions avoid bulky trays and putty-like materials, making the process easier and more pleasant for most patients.

2. Faster Procedure

Scanning usually takes only a few minutes. If an area is missed, the dentist can immediately rescan that part rather than repeating the whole impression. This saves chairside time and reduces patient inconvenience.

3. Better Accuracy

Patients benefit from improved accuracy because digital scans can reduce errors caused by:

* Material distortion
* Air bubbles
* Improper tray seating

More accurate impressions may lead to better-fitting crowns, bridges, aligners, dentures, and restorations.

4. Reduced Anxiety

🦷 Why are my teeth sensitive to hot or cold?

Do you feel a sharp pain when sipping hot coffee ☕ or enjoying ice cream 🍦? You might be dealing with tooth sensitivity.

👉 Common reasons include:
• Worn-out enamel (due to aggressive brushing or acidic foods)
• Gum recession exposing the root surface
• Tooth decay or cavities
• Cracked or chipped teeth
• Recent dental treatments (temporary sensitivity is normal)

The inner layer of your tooth (dentin) gets exposed, allowing heat or cold to reach the nerve — causing that sudden discomfort.

👉 How can you manage it?
✔ Use a desensitizing toothpaste
✔ Avoid very acidic or sugary foods
✔ Brush gently with a soft-bristle brush
✔ Don’t ignore persistent sensitivity
